an3.103:1.1: This is one of several times that the Buddha spoke of his meditation before enlightenment (see eg. [mn4](), [mn19](), [mn128]()). In these texts the Buddha takes pains to depict himself as an ordinary person who struggled with the same issues in meditation as anyone else. | “Sworn to awakening” is _bodhisatta_, and such passages as this are apparently the original context for this term. The Pali _satta_ represents a number of different words in Sanskrit. The standard rendering _sattva_ is grammatically odd (“awakening-being”); it suggests there is a completeness about this state, but the phrase here emphasizes it is incomplete. I read as equivalent to _śapta_ (“sworn to”), which is more familiar in the sense “curse”, but is also used in the sense of swearing an oath in a legal case (Manu 8.109–116). Related terms appear in the Suttas in this sense ([sn11.7:3.1](), [ud4.8:15.2]()), and the exact form *satta* occurs at [ja422:14.1](). In such cases, the oath always implies some kind of negative consequences should it fail. I believe that oath is the one referred to at [an2.5:1.4](), where the Buddha says that he determined to realize awakening or die trying.
